## Docket 1.2.7

**A page served only the site furniture was served no content.**

Some pages come back containing the menu and footer that appear on every page,
and nothing of their own between them — a page whose content is built by
JavaScript that did not run, or a cache returning a shell under load. Docket
already noticed this when many pages did it at once. It now notices when a
single page does, which is the case nothing could see before: that page was
being judged on its navigation's word count, headings and links, and no finding
said so.

The site's furniture is worked out from the site itself — the phrases that
recur across its pages — so it needs no assumption about how the site is built.
Measured against nine live pages of a real site: ordinary pages score between
0.000 and 0.009 against that furniture, and a page that is nothing but the
furniture scores 0.978.

Pages in that state are no longer judged for content they were never given, and
they are reported rather than quietly dropped. Docket says what it received and
points at Search Console's URL Inspection for what Google receives, rather than
guessing on your behalf.
